quiz.title: Unit 3 FRQ 4: Polar functions (Topics 3.8 to 3.15)
quiz.headline: Convert a point on a polar graph to rectangular coordinates, find where the graph meets the origin, use an average rate of change of r, and decide whether the distance from the origin is increasing.
quiz.promptTitle: Free response 4 · Polar functions · graphing calculator
quiz.prompt: The polar function r = f(θ) is given by f(θ) = 1 + 3 cos θ for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. The graph of r = f(θ) in polar coordinates and the graph of f in the θr-plane are shown.
quiz.instructions: Part A style: a graphing calculator is required. Show the work that leads to each answer; answers without supporting work may not earn credit where work is requested. Angle measures are in radians. Avoid rounding intermediate values, and give decimal approximations accurate to three places after the decimal point unless the part says otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.
quiz.note: Original practice question written in the AP Precalculus free-response format (6 points, parts A to C). Scoring is self-assessed with the point-by-point rubric. It is not an official AP question or an official AP score.

stimulusBlocks.caption: Graph of r = 1 + 3 cos θ in polar coordinates
stimulusBlocks.alt: A limaçon on a polar grid. Its outer loop reaches 4 units along the polar axis, and a small inner loop passes through the origin and reaches 2 units along the polar axis.

stimulusBlocks.caption: Graph of r = f(θ) in the θr-plane
stimulusBlocks.alt: A cosine-shaped curve from r = 4 at θ = 0, decreasing to r = −2 at θ = π, and increasing back to 4 at θ = 2π. It crosses r = 0 twice.

scaffold.label: Show work
scaffold.text: Write the setup, such as the expression you evaluate or the equation you solve, before the answer.

scaffold.label: Use exact values
scaffold.text: Without a calculator, give exact values such as √3/2 or 7π/6, not decimals.

scaffold.label: Justify
scaffold.text: When a part says give a reason or explain, refer to the graph, the given values, or the context.

responseFields.label: Part A (i)
responseFields.prompt: A (i). Find the rectangular coordinates (x, y) of the point on the graph of r = f(θ) that corresponds to θ = 2π/3. In which quadrant is this point?
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part A (ii)
responseFields.prompt: A (ii). Find all values of θ, for 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, at which the graph of r = f(θ) passes through the origin.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Where a polar graph meets the origin

responseFields.label: Part B (i)
responseFields.prompt: B (i). Find the average rate of change of r with respect to θ over the interval 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Average rate of change of r

responseFields.label: Part B (ii)
responseFields.prompt: B (ii). Interpret the meaning of your answer to B (i) in terms of the signed radius.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Interpreting the average rate of change

responseFields.label: Part C (i)
responseFields.prompt: C (i). Let α be the value of θ in the interval 0 < θ < π for which f(θ) = 0. On the interval α < θ < π, is the distance between the point (f(θ), θ) and the origin increasing or decreasing?
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (ii)
responseFields.prompt: C (ii). Give a reason for your answer to C (i).
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Sign of r and direction of change

rubric.label: A (i) Rectangular coordinates and quadrant
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for (x, y) = (0.250, −0.433), exactly (1/4, −√3/4), in Quadrant IV.

rubric.label: A (ii) Values of θ
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for θ = arccos(−1/3) ≈ 1.911 and θ = 2π − arccos(−1/3) ≈ 4.373. Both are needed.

rubric.label: B (ii) Interpretation
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: on average, the signed radius decreases by about 1.910 units per radian as θ increases from 0 to π/2.

rubric.label: C (i) Increasing or decreasing
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: the distance is increasing.

rubric.label: C (ii) Reason
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: on α < θ < π, f(θ) is negative and decreasing (cos θ is decreasing), so |f(θ)| is increasing.

quiz.modelResponse:
A (i). f(2π/3) = 1 + 3(−1/2) = −1/2. Then x = r cos θ = (−1/2)(−1/2) = 1/4 = 0.250 and y = r sin θ = (−1/2)(√3/2) = −√3/4 ≈ −0.433. The point (0.250, −0.433) is in Quadrant IV.

A (ii). The graph passes through the origin when r = 0: 1 + 3 cos θ = 0, so cos θ = −1/3. θ = arccos(−1/3) ≈ 1.911 and θ = 2π − arccos(−1/3) ≈ 4.373.

B (i). f(0) = 4 and f(π/2) = 1. The average rate of change is (1 − 4)/(π/2 − 0) = −6/π ≈ −1.910.

B (ii). As θ increases from 0 to π/2, the signed radius decreases, on average, by about 1.910 units per radian.

C (i). The distance between the point and the origin is increasing.

C (ii). On α < θ < π, cos θ < −1/3, so f(θ) < 0. cos θ is decreasing on this interval, so f(θ) is decreasing. A polar function that is negative and decreasing moves away from the origin, so the distance |f(θ)| is increasing.
quiz.alternateModel: In C (ii), you may read the θr-graph: on (α, π) the curve is below the θ-axis and falling, so its values move farther from 0.
commonErrors: Plotting the point at θ = 2π/3 in Quadrant II, ignoring that r is negative.
Dividing by 90 or by 1 instead of π/2 in B (i).
Interpreting −1.910 as the point moving 1.910 units closer to the origin per radian.
Concluding the distance decreases because r is decreasing, without checking the sign of r.
